claims.statement: NACP applies admission only to PUT/POST register, update, plan, and validate routes and proxies other requests; update and plan matching accepts any non-slash job ID, so direct access to Nomad bypasses NACP enforcement.

The CLI uses defaults only when -config is omitted or empty, does not search for a conventional file, and fails startup for an explicitly missing or invalid config path; bootstrap logging is info-level stdout text or JSON selected by -bootstrap-json-logger.

HCL is decoded over defaults with top-level bind and port, defaulting to 0.0.0.0:6464, Nomad http://localhost:4646, no TLS or OPA SDK, and empty controller lists; an empty HCL file retains these defaults.
Default logging is info-level text on stdout with JSON disabled and its destination defaulting to stdout; OTEL logging, metrics, tracing, and per-controller resolve_token are disabled by default.

HCL loading applies a max_sig_attempts default of 50 to zero-valued Notation configurations, including nested opa_rule blocks on mutators and validators, while validation requires a positive effective value and trust policy/store paths.

NACP uses an empty HCL evaluation context and passes local rule, SDK config, TLS, and trust-policy paths directly to filesystem APIs rather than resolving them relative to the config file; relative paths therefore depend on the process working directory.
Controllers require type and name labels, nonblank names, and unique names within each controller kind; construction preserves each list's order, and admission runs mutators before validators.

Supported HCL mutators are opa_json_patch, json_patch_webhook, and opa_bundle_json_patch; validators are opa, webhook, opa_bundle, and notation, each requiring its corresponding rule, webhook, or notation block.

Local OPA controllers require nonblank filename and query; bundle controllers require an opa_sdk_rule decision path and a shared opa_sdk with nonblank ID and config_path; webhook controllers require an absolute HTTP(S) endpoint and a nonblank syntactically valid method.

Configuration validation runs after HCL decoding and again in buildServer, checking port 1..65535, nonblank bind, effective Nomad configuration and absolute HTTP(S) address, listener cert/key presence, upstream cert/key pairing, and controller requirements; the loader additionally restricts slog destinations to stdout or stderr.

Startup validation is not exhaustive: it does not prove bind availability, remote connectivity, or file contents, and unsupported logging levels reach a panic in logger construction rather than a Validate error; supported levels are case-insensitive debug, info, warn, and error.

NACP must be placed on a restricted control-plane network with listener and upstream TLS; configured webhooks and bundle services are trusted policy infrastructure, credentials belong outside source control, and insecure_skip_verify and repo_plain_http are reserved for controlled development.

NACP trusts the trimmed first X-Forwarded-For entry without authenticating the sender, otherwise deriving client IP from RemoteAddr with a raw-string fallback; that IP is included in policy context and webhook client-IP headers, requiring trusted-edge sanitization.

Top-level listener TLS uses cert_file and key_file and defaults to server-only TLS without a CA file; a nonempty ca_file enables RequireAndVerifyClientCert unless no_client_cert is true, and listener TLS has a TLS 1.2 minimum.

Nested nomad.tls configures a separate upstream transport with TLS 1.2 minimum, optional client certificate pair, custom CA or system roots, and insecure_skip_verify; this transport also serves ACL self-lookups, and the Nomad URL scheme selects HTTPS.

Both TLS HCL blocks require ca_file, cert_file, and key_file attributes syntactically, although empty values support runtime configurations such as CA-only upstream TLS; supplied CA PEM must contain a valid certificate, and custom upstream roots replace rather than augment the system pool.

Tag pushes run a release workflow that imports GPG credentials, logs into GHCR, and invokes GoReleaser; release configuration builds CGO-disabled Linux, Windows, and Darwin binaries, tar.gz or Windows ZIP archives, signed checksums.txt, and latest plus release-tag GHCR images.

The release Dockerfile consumes a prebuilt nacp binary and runs /nacp in scratch as UID/GID 10001:10001 with a system CA bundle from Alpine, while dev.Dockerfile compiles source with CGO disabled and runs the binary as nobody in Ubuntu.

Release deployments must provision configuration, policies, SDK configuration, TLS keys/certificates, and Notation trust/credential resources at readable runtime paths for UID/GID 10001:10001; the scratch image's system CA bundle does not provision application policy or private signing trust material.

The demo Nomad job renders nacp.conf, Rego, and opa.yml into allocation paths and starts NACP with /local/nacp.conf.hcl; nacp.conf is a Nomad template, not raw NACP HCL, and discovery loops can render duplicate fixed controller names that validation rejects.

NACP exposes no CPU/memory resource fields in its HCL schema; the demo's CPU/memory block belongs to monitoring, and its NACP service registration has no health check. Admission request size caps are not process-memory caps because decoding, patching, and validator job copies allocate additional data.

run registers SIGINT/SIGTERM, installs configured logging, optionally initializes telemetry, then creates one shared OPA SDK before upstream transport, controllers, and HTTP server construction; listener startup is attempted only after these steps succeed.

OPA SDK startup opens its configuration and waits on the SDK Ready channel with a 30-second signal-derived context; sdk.New receives the parent context rather than the readiness context, and readiness timeout or cancellation stops the SDK before returning an error.

Controller construction reads and prepares local Rego and constructs Notation verifiers, so unreadable or invalid rule/trust-policy files can fail server construction; trust-store usability and registry verification can also fail later during admission.

The installed NACP handler has no dedicated readiness endpoint and the process has no live HCL reload path; the Starting NACP log is emitted before ListenAndServe or ListenAndServeTLS succeeds, so startup logs and passthrough responses alone do not prove policy readiness.

NACP caps recognized admission request bodies at 32 MiB, webhook response bodies at 10 MiB, webhook HTTP requests at 30 seconds, and ACL self-lookups at 30 seconds; outbound webhook and ACL calls also carry the incoming request context.

The HTTP server sets ReadHeaderTimeout to 15 seconds, ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout to 310 seconds, and IdleTimeout to 120 seconds; the Nomad transport uses 310 seconds for dial timeout, dialer keepalive, and TLS handshake, not an overall forwarding http.Client timeout.

SIGINT/SIGTERM triggers HTTP shutdown with a fresh 30-second context, followed by deferred OPA stop with its own 10-second context and then telemetry cleanup with context.Background and no NACP deadline; this is not one generic 30-second shutdown budget.

http.ErrServerClosed is a normal return, HTTP drain failures propagate, telemetry cleanup errors are joined to run's result, and main exits status 1 for configuration/runtime errors; NACP stopped can be logged before deferred cleanup finishes.

Any controller requesting resolve_token enables identity lookup on actionable admission routes; empty tokens skip lookup, while failed GET /v1/acl/token/self transport/status/JSON handling returns HTTP 500 and aborts admission and forwarding.

Resolved ACL policy context uses ACLTokenContext instead of the full token, omitting SecretID and ExpirationTTL and populating ResolveToken according to whether resolution was requested; existing consumers of removed fields require migration.
Webhook handling rejects non-2xx, oversized, unreadable, or undecodable responses; validator errors and JSON-patch mutator errors become admission failures rather than being ignored.

Admission decoding and register/plan controller errors use writeError's HTTP 500 rather than specialized body-limit status handling; the validate route can attach validator errors to the successful upstream validation response instead of aborting forwarding.

Warning and validation-error injection is limited to successful Nomad responses, preserving non-2xx upstream bodies; decoding or rewriting failures on eligible responses produce Preparing response failed and return a proxy response-modification error.

OPA bundle validators fail on non-object decisions and non-null errors/warnings values that are not lists of strings, while absent or null message fields are accepted; this stricter decision contract is an Unreleased upgrade risk.

Validators evaluate isolated job copies of the final mutator output; the Unreleased changelog identifies corrected mutation/validation ordering, route matching, token sanitization, startup validation, and webhook failure handling as compatibility/security changes.

The current Unreleased changelog calls for migration from log_level to telemetry.logging.level, rechecking custom Rego for OPA 1.19 assignment safety, and updating log consumers for slog/OTEL changes; it also records release-image CA provisioning and numeric non-root identity changes.

Focused regression tests cover explicit missing config paths, route matching, config validation/defaults, token sanitization, OPA SDK setup and readiness timeout, and generated TLS configurations; the shutdown test specifically exercises SIGINT with default and enabled telemetry, not every SIGTERM or drain failure scenario.
